newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks off highs amid some wariness.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks off highs amid some wariness.

text.p: Madrid stock indices were off highs at midsession on Wednesday, pulling back as an element of caution came into the market, dealers said.
The general index rose 4.98 points, 0.82 percent, to 613.56 and the Ibex was up 49.11 points, 0.7 percent, to 7,019.03.

Short and medium term the outlook is positive, despite the fact that many shares are near, if not above, their fair value. This is because of the continued flow of Spanish savings towards investment funds amid lower key money rates. These funds have to invest in stocks regardless, they said.
Repsol was most heavily traded stock, pushing up after a large sell order came to an end, dealers said. Repsol was up 130 pesetas to 6,430.

A trader at BSN said: "There's no (Repsol) news on the corporate side, simply the big seller we had in the market in the past couple of weeks has disappeared. It could be related to the privatisation of (Italy's) ENI."
Other dealers said some investors had switched from Repsol into ENI during the latter's privatisation, and were now buying Repsol again.

Viscofan, which re-entered the Ibex on Tuesday, was again among the big climbers, rising 90 pesetas to 3,600. Analysts said most of its sales are denominated in dollars, and it thus seen benefitting from the greenback's appreciation against the peseta.
